CONFIDENCE 80 — Step 6 classification table, line 209: the row 'Every point wrong by a clean factor of two or one half' lists 'peak against RMS' as a usual cause alongside 'single-ended against differential' and 'amplitude against peak-to-peak'. Peak-to-RMS is not a clean factor of two for any common waveform — it is sqrt(2) (~1.414x) for a sinusoid, 1x for a square wave, sqrt(3) (~1.73x) for a triangle. An engineer using this decision table to diagnose a genuine 2x discrepancy who checks 'peak vs RMS' first is checking the wrong thing; a real peak/RMS confusion would show up as a ~1.4x error, not 2x, and would be misfiled by this table's own logic. Fix: drop 'peak against RMS' from this row, or move it to its own row with the correct sqrt(2)-class factor.

hallucination_risks: CONFIDENCE 82 — Gotchas, lines 276-280: 'Verilog-AMS `wreal` carries explicit unknown and high-impedance states for exactly this; a plain SystemVerilog `real` does not, so a user-defined net type needs its own validity field...' This is stated as flat, universal fact, not a [[FILL:]] slot, yet it is not true of the standard Verilog-AMS `wreal` net type as specified by the Accellera LRM: an undriven `wreal` defaults to 0.0, exactly the same ambiguous-zero problem the bullet opens by describing ('An undriven real net is worth 0.0, and nothing tells you which zero you have'). wrealXstate/wrealZstate exist only as a vendor/patented extension (found in Cadence patent literature), not as a guaranteed base-language feature — this is precisely the kind of tool-specific fact rule 2 says the author cannot know and must not assert. As written the bullet contradicts itself: it sets up 'nothing tells you which zero you have' as the danger, then claims wreal solves it, when per the standard LRM it does not. This is exactly the sentence in the 'most valuable section' that would make an AMS methodology owner distrust the rest of the file. Fix: either cite this as team-specific tool behaviour behind a [[FILL:]], or state plainly that base wreal has the same undriven-zero ambiguity as plain real unless the team's specific flow adds a validity/strength extension.

recheck.why: Lint is 1.000 clean, 260 lines, role/level exact (ams-verification-engineer/senior), all 9 slots spent, Grep/Read budget arithmetic exact (7 Greps allocated and 7 spent; 6 Reads allocated and 6 spent), vocabulary conformant, and the AMS domain content is correct. But the skill's central output column has no source: `modelled : <value the model produces, with unit and where it came from>` is assigned by NO step. Grepping the file, "modelled" appears only in the output framing (line 25), the fenced block (line 198) and the verification checklist (line 246) — never in a procedure step. `delta` inherits the gap, and with it the whole in-band/out-of-band classification, since a band test needs both numbers. The asymmetry is decisive: the analog reference side gets a dedicated slot (Circuit-sim measurement export), a dedicated handoff step 5 ("Ask the analog design owner to run the circuit simulation ... and to save the extracted measurements where they can be read from disk"), one Grep and two Reads. The model's own side gets no slot for where an RNM run's output lands, no handoff asking anyone to run the real-number model, and no budgeted Grep or Read to read it. Step 3's parameter-block Read yields declared constants, not "the value the model produces" at a stimulus condition. Step 6 is therefore unrunnable, and its shape table proves the omission is structural not a wording slip — "Exactly 0.0 where the value should be non-zero", "Correct at DC, wrong on every transition", "Only after a long run, growing slowly" are observations of RNM runtime behaviour the agent has no sanctioned path to. An engineer following this either writes `?` in `modelled` for every row (the skill produces no correlation at all) or improvises by hand-evaluating the model source — precisely the fabricated evidence lines 59-60 call worse than none, and which step 4 already forbids in the adjacent case. This is the verb-honesty failure the pack's rule 1 exists to catch: a run the agent cannot perform, with no explicit handoff, sitting under the deliverable the description promises.

Then re-balance the budget: the new file needs a Grep and at least one bounded Read, so the current 7-Grep / 6-Read caps and their per-step allocation must be restated to account for them.
